Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
incertitudes: Q4(c) : les solutions de cos θ + sin θ = 1 (θ = 2nπ ou π/2 + 2nπ) sont précisément les valeurs où f(θ), telle qu'imprimée (tan θ et cot θ), n'est pas définie. Le corrigé donne la réponse attendue par l'identité (a)-(b) et signale que, stricto sensu, l'équation f(θ) = 1 n'a alors aucune solution.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Express tangent and cotangent in terms of sine and cosine (valid when $\sin\theta \ne 0$ and $\cos\theta \ne 0$):
$$1 - \tan\theta = \frac{\cos\theta - \sin\theta}{\cos\theta}, \qquad 1 - \cot\theta = \frac{\sin\theta - \cos\theta}{\sin\theta}.$$
Hence
$$\frac{\cos\theta}{1 - \tan\theta} = \frac{\cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta - \sin\theta}, \qquad \frac{\sin\theta}{1 - \cot\theta} = \frac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta - \cos\theta} = -\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta - \sin\theta}.$$
Add:
$$f(\theta) = \frac{\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta - \sin\theta} = \frac{(\cos\theta - \sin\theta)(\cos\theta + \sin\theta)}{\cos\theta - \sin\theta} = \cos\theta + \sin\theta,$$
the cancellation being legitimate because $\cos\theta - \sin\theta \ne 0$ (that is $\tan\theta \ne 1$, which is needed for $f$ to be defined).
$$\boxed{f(\theta) \equiv \cos\theta + \sin\theta}$$
The identity holds for all $\theta$ at which $f(\theta)$ is defined, i.e. $\theta \ne \frac{n\pi}{2}$ and $\theta \ne \frac\pi4 + n\pi$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $f(\theta) = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{1 - \tan\theta} + \dfrac{\sin\theta}{1 - \cot\theta}$ (so that $f(\theta) \equiv \cos\theta + \sin\theta$), express $f(\theta)$ in the form $R\sin(\theta + \lambda)$, where $R > 0$ and $\lambda$ is an acute angle. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Expand $R\sin(\theta + \lambda) = R\cos\lambda\,\sin\theta + R\sin\lambda\,\cos\theta$ and compare with $\cos\theta + \sin\theta$:
$$R\cos\lambda = 1 \;(\text{coefficient of }\sin\theta), \qquad R\sin\lambda = 1 \;(\text{coefficient of }\cos\theta).$$
Squaring and adding: $R^2 = 1 + 1 = 2$, so $R = \sqrt2$ ($R > 0$). Dividing: $\tan\lambda = 1$, so $\lambda = \dfrac\pi4$ ($45^\circ$), which is acute and consistent with $\cos\lambda, \sin\lambda > 0$.
$$\boxed{f(\theta) = \sqrt2\,\sin\!\left(\theta + \frac\pi4\right)}$$
Check at $\theta = 0$: $\sqrt2\sin\frac\pi4 = 1 = \cos 0 + \sin 0$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $f(\theta) = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{1 - \tan\theta} + \dfrac{\sin\theta}{1 - \cot\theta}$, find the general solutions of the equation $f(\theta) = 1$. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Using part (a), $f(\theta) = 1$ becomes $\cos\theta + \sin\theta = 1$, and by part (b)
$$\sqrt2\sin\!\left(\theta + \frac\pi4\right) = 1 \;\Rightarrow\; \sin\!\left(\theta + \frac\pi4\right) = \frac{1}{\sqrt2}.$$
The general solutions of $\sin A = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$ are $A = \dfrac\pi4 + 2n\pi$ or $A = \dfrac{3\pi}{4} + 2n\pi$, $n \in \mathbb{Z}$. With $A = \theta + \frac\pi4$:
$$\theta + \frac\pi4 = \frac\pi4 + 2n\pi \;\Rightarrow\; \theta = 2n\pi, \qquad \theta + \frac\pi4 = \frac{3\pi}{4} + 2n\pi \;\Rightarrow\; \theta = \frac\pi2 + 2n\pi.$$
$$\boxed{\theta = 2n\pi \ \text{ or } \ \theta = 2n\pi + \frac\pi2, \quad n \in \mathbb{Z}}$$
(in degrees, $\theta = 360^\circ n$ or $\theta = 90^\circ + 360^\circ n$.) Check: $\cos 0 + \sin 0 = 1$ and $\cos\frac\pi2 + \sin\frac\pi2 = 1$.

**Remark on the printed function.** These are the solutions of $\cos\theta + \sin\theta = 1$, which is what the question intends. However, the original expression $f(\theta)$ is not defined at $\theta = 2n\pi$ ($\cot\theta$ undefined) nor at $\theta = \frac\pi2 + 2n\pi$ ($\tan\theta$ undefined), so strictly, as the function is written, the equation $f(\theta) = 1$ has no value of $\theta$ at which it is satisfied; the answer above is the expected one from the simplified form.
